thread.title: Weekly Market Preview: Labor Day Edition (AMZN, WDAY, DOCU, AVGO, PANW)

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Weekly Market Preview: Labor Day Edition (AMZN, WDAY, DOCU, AVGO, PANW)
text:
Shutterstock photo The stock market will be closed Monday for the Labor Day holiday, but the action (and volatility) is poised to ramp back up on Tuesday.
When the market resumes Tuesday, investors will be reminded of ongoing tariff drama between the U.S. and its trading partners that still beed to be sorted out. So far, the bulls have not allowed trade rhetoric to force them to relinquish control of this market. But there are several other topics to keep an eye on. Speaking of labor, the Labor Department will issue its monthly jobs report this coming week.
Economists are targeting non-farm payrolls to rise to 187,000 jobs (up from last month’s 157,000). While that number would keep the unemployment rate steady at 3.9%, will it be enough? The result will no doubt have a profound impact on equities, which many analysts believe are trading way overpriced. Among them is Amazon ( AMZN ), which — now trading north to $2,000 per share (up 72% year to date — is an eyelash away from the $1T market cap. Its cap is $981.68B, to be exact.
The e-commerce giant, which is still rising since its Q2 earnings report, would join Apple ( AAPL ) as the only publicly-traded companies to achieve the $1T status. This week, investors will also focus on the earnings calendar not only to gauge the continued strength of corporate profits, but also for continued signs that earnings multiples and equity valuations are justified. Here are four stocks to keep an eye on.
Workday ( WDAY ) - Reports after the close, Tuesday, September 4
Wall Street expects the company to earn 26 cents per share on revenue of $663.09 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to 24 cents per share on revenue of $525.32 million.
What to Watch: The maker of human resources software has grown to become a top player not only in Cloud applications for financial management, but also areas such as human capital management, payroll and analytics. Despite what has become a highly competitive market, led by Salesforce ( CRM ), Workday continues to find ways to grow, producing revenue of $619 million Q2, up by 29% year over year and surpassing Wall Street forecasts by $9.8 million. Notably, subscription revenue surged 31%. But with the stock trading at all-time highs, expectations also reflects this performance.
DocuSign ( DOCU ) - Reports after the close, Wednesday, September 5
Wall Street expects the company to earn 1 cent per share on revenue of $159.6 million. This will be the company’s first earnings report since its IPO earlier this year.
What to Watch: One of the most successful IPOs of the year, DocuSign provides individuals and businesses the ability to digitize an agreement process. DocuSign competes HelloSign and Adobe ( ADBE ) Sign, among others. Despite the crowded market, the company’s client base — which includes the likes of T-Mobile ( TMUS ), Salesforce, Morgan Stanley ( MS ) and Bank of America ( BAC ) — has grown to more than 370,000 users and more than 300 of the Fortune 500 companies. With such a strong portfolio of customers, DocuSign on Thursday must now outline its path towards profitability.
Broadcom ( AVGO ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, September 6
Wall Street expects the company to earn $4.82 per share on revenue of $5.07 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came came to $4.10 per share on revenue of $4.47 billion.
What to Watch: Broadcom shares have taken a beating over the past three months, falling more than 14%, while both the Nasdaq and S&P 500 have notched all-time highs. The decline was driven by the company’s announcement to buy CA Inc. ( CA ) for $19 billion. To the extent the management on Thursday can sell investors on the benefits of the deal, while outlining improving business conditions, the stock could rebound strongly. Combined with a strong top- and bottom-line beat, Broadcom’s decline could be a thing of the past, especially with Apple’s ( AAPL ) new iPhone’s — to which it provides wireless components — due to be released.
Palo Alto Network ( PANW ) - Reports after the close, Thursday, September 6
Wall Street expects the company to earn $1.17 per share on revenue of $633.05 million. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings came to 92 cents per share on revenue of $509.1 million.
What to Watch: New product launches for both network and cloud-based applications continue to strengthened Palo Alto’s revenue which impressively by 31% in the second quarter. And despite intense competition from the likes of Check Point ( CHKP ), Cisco ( CSCO ) and Fortinet ( FTNT ) in the firewall security market, the fact that Palo Alto’s revenue and profits continue are accelerating each quarter underscores the strength of its best-of-class status. But with the stock trading at all-time highs, valuation concerns have emerged.
